samples.summary: Design doc still describes group export as unconditional `<p:grpSp>` emission; the new whole-group drop is undocumented
samples.evidence: docs/design/slides/slides-pptx-export.md:194 states Group → `<p:grpSp>` with "recurse" and no drop condition, and the Non-Goals section (lines 62-66) documents only that a *chart* is silently dropped. After this delta, `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:122` also drops the enclosing `GroupElement` (and, recursively, whole ancestor chains) when every child serializes to ''. The round-trip fidelity contract in the same doc (lines 18-26, "every element type … is written back") now has a second, undocumented exception: a group whose only children are charts or fetch-failed images vanishes from the deck entirely. Doc lives under docs/design/<topic>/ so no lane checks it. Fix belongs in the doc, not the new code.

samples.summary: `groupToXml`'s TSDoc contract does not state it can now return an empty string
samples.evidence: The doc comment at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:82-92 (and the module header at lines 1-22) still describe `groupToXml` as emitting a `<p:grpSp>`; nothing in the published contract tells a caller the return can be ''. Only in-repo caller is `elementToXml` (group.ts:73) → `slideToXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:157), both of which tolerate '' (join over strings, and an spTree with only SPTREE_ROOT is valid), so this is documentation drift rather than a broken caller. `ElementXmlCtx.resolveImageRId` (group.ts:33-38) documents its own drop semantics, so the asymmetry is visible.

samples.summary: Animations targeting a now-dropped group are silently discarded (verified benign, no invalid spid emitted)
samples.evidence: Checked the invariant this delta could break: `slideToXml` builds `spidMap` by regexing the *emitted* body (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:110-123), so a group dropped by group.ts:122 never enters the map. `animationsToTimingXml` handles the miss with `if (spid === undefined) continue;` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/animation.ts:321-325) and elides the click group when it empties (line 325), so no dangling `spTgt spid` reaches the file. Connector export emits no `stCxn`/`endCxn` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/connector.ts:112-126), and image/hyperlink rels are added lazily inside the resolvers (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:305-333), so a dropped group also leaves no orphan relationship. Reporting only so the panel knows the consumers were checked; the silent loss of the animation is not surfaced to `onImageError` callers such as packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:22.

finding.summary: A group whose only children are dropped images now serializes as a childless `<p:grpSp>`
finding.evidence: `elementToXml` returns `''` for an image whose rId resolved to `null` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:65). `groupToXml` builds its children with `data.children.map(...).join('')` and unconditionally wraps them (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:115-117), so a group element containing only image children whose fetch failed emits `<p:grpSp>` with `nvGrpSpPr`/`grpSpPr` and no shape children. An empty group shape tree is not what the writer previously could produce (the old resolver threw instead), and PowerPoint commonly reports such a part as needing repair. The fix belongs in `groupToXml` (skip a group that serialized no children) rather than at the new `null` return.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `groupToXml` unconditionally wraps its joined children, so a group whose only children are dropped images emits a childless `<p:grpSp>`. The code does not read that way: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/group.ts:122` contains `if (!children) return '';` — the exact fix the finding proposes — with a comment at lines 117-121 naming this very case ("Every child serialized away (dropped images, Phase-2 charts)... Drop the group itself"). Since `elementToXml` returns `''` for a dropped image (line 66) and for a nested group that itself serialized nothing (line 73 -> 122), `children` is the empty string in the described scenario and no `<p:grpSp>` is emitted. Grep across `packages/slides/src` confirms group.ts:124 is the only site emitting `<p:grpSp>` for a `GroupElement`; the other `<p:grpSpPr>` hits (slide.ts:53/229, layout.ts:74, master.ts:44, index.ts:436/464) are the fixed spTree-level group properties, not element groups, so there is no bypassing emission path. The described defective code is not present.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason:
This "finding" is not a claim about any code in the repository — it is the harness's own run-failure placeholder, reproduced verbatim. The outer text is the string `lensFailureSummary` emits when a lens throws (`scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1695`: "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: ${…err.message}"), and the inner text is exactly the message built by `poolExhaustedError` (`scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-636`: "${label}: every credential in the pool (${pool.size}) was retired — nothing left to fail over to", kind "pool-exhausted"). The synthesised blocking record is created at `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:2757-2778`. So what happened is that a review lens ran out of Anthropic credentials mid-run and never produced a verdict; the "finding" carries no file, no symbol, and no location.

Nothing in it is a blast-radius claim: it names no changed contract, no caller left on an old signature, no removed/renamed export, no invariant, and no path that bypasses a new guard. There is no bypassing site to cite because none is alleged. Under this lens's rubric there is nothing to review.

The repository also treats this exact string as an infrastructure signal handled on a separate path, not as a code finding: `scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:561-565` matches the same prefix and comments "Their blocking finding is an infrastructure signal, not a review finding … the guard already pages separately on the INFRA path", and `scripts/agent/review-round-guard.mjs:188` pages a human with the "invalid-verdict" reason. So dropping this item from the merge gate does not silence the failure — the round guard still escalates it.

(Noted while checking, but explicitly NOT the finding as raised and not something I am asserting as a blocking defect here: `poolExhaustedError` does not set `err.infra`, and `err.infra` is only set from an API-error match at `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:2740`, so a pool-exhausted crash takes the non-infra branch at line 1691 and is published as an ordinary blocking finding rather than an infra record. That is a separate observation about the harness, and it is why this malformed item reached me at all.)
